body:
Released skgo v0.17.0 (`b3aae63e4ddf98e282a7c3539e7288cd18ba2d2f`), adapter 0.17.0 and Kit 3.0.0 build a `router.type: 'hash'` app, but the embedded Go server still selects the requested pathname and renders its page. The current complete project measurement independently demonstrates this without relying on the browser history timeout: - Ordinary HTTP `GET /about` returns 200 HTML containing the authored `HASH_ROUTER_ABOUT_42` page literal. - The document response for `/about#/about` has the same authored About SSR content. The fragment is absent from the HTTP request, so this is another `/about` document request. - Each retained document body is 3,966 bytes. The independent app-template marker is `HASH_ROUTER_SHELL_42`; the shell contract also requires Kit's native start/app imports and no authored Home/About page content. - Root client boot, native `#/about` navigation and Back work. Forward/reload time out, but attribution of that separate browser result awaits a stock Kit oracle; it is not needed to establish this Go document-handler defect. Reproduction uses the actual released CLI and canonical VP build: 1. Generate a minimal TypeScript project with `skgo new -skgo-version v0.17.0 -module example.com/hash -- --template minimal --types ts --add vitest=usages:unit`. 2. Set `router: { type: 'hash' }` in the existing `sveltekit({...})` configuration. Put `

HASH_ROUTER_HOME_42

About` in the root page, and `

HASH_ROUTER_ABOUT_42

Home` in `src/routes/about/+page.svelte`. Add the independent shell marker in `src/app.html`. 3. Run `vp build`, compile and serve the ordinary embedded Go application on its owned origin, and request `/about` directly. Expected: a hash-routed build serves its client app shell for document pathname requests, with SSR/prerender disabled under Kit's hash-router contract. JavaScript-off visitors receive that shell; the native client renders the hash-selected page. Preserve ordinary pathname-router behavior and Go-owned endpoint/static-asset handling. Include a real embedded-server regression with literal shell/page expectations and retain the existing native history check separately. Public evidence: [complete measurement 37246997393](https://github.com/tylergannon/skgo-project/actions/runs/37246997393), source revision `4474bb45079e959c0d18af9c6fc074d4c9fa731f`. The source-check artifact contains `router-modes-artifacts/hash/http-about.body.html`, `http-about.headers.txt`, `browser-deep-about.body.html` and `browser-requests.json`. Existing [project matrix issue #121](https://github.com/tylergannon/skgo-project/issues/121) tracks both hash mode and the separate server-resolution refusal. This core issue is scoped to the independently demonstrated document-shell behavior; it adds no matrix cell and claims no repair.

comments.body:
**Triage — 2026-10-18**

Checked against current [`main` at `920b6aca`](https://github.com/tylergannon/skgo/tree/920b6aca738a65d6c046a67f4db2373596fafd03). Classification: `bounded-hard`. 

The current adapter manifest/document path still has no explicit hash-router shell selection, so the production document concern remains relevant after the development rewrite. Keep this scoped to the independently demonstrated pathname document-shell contract, preserving Go endpoints/assets and ordinary pathname mode. Browser Forward/reload attribution remains a separate oracle question; do not bundle it into the core fix.

title: Hash-routed builds render pathname pages instead of the client shell
